title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a table of contents, not a page of proofs. It continues the index of the unpublished 'Deuxième partie : Variations sur l'équation des lacets' of La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), manuscript pages 390–550. It lists the sub-headings of §46 and the whole of §§47–48. The problem served is the one Grothendieck pursued from §38 on: describe the outer action of Γ_Q (and, more generally, of 'automorphismes-lacets') on the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1−{0,1,∞}. He does this through 'loop equations' (équations des lacets) and through a comparison π'_{0,3} ≅ Ĝ^+_{0,3}, a congruence/modular group related to SL(2,Z)' and SL(2,Ẑ)'. Groups of pairs or triples of parameters (λ or μ, f, α, β, …) satisfying these equations then appear. In modern language they are proto-versions of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: GT^ (in Drinfeld 1990) and its 'genus 1 / M_{1,1}' variants.

§46 'Notations définitives', continued:
- I. Defines groups M_{0,3}^~ and N_{0,3}^{!~}.
- II. Computes elements of N^{!~}_{0,3} in four equivalent parametrisations: (f,g,h), (α_0,β_0,f), (α,β,f), (ξ,η,f). These are 1-cocycle data on cyclic groups, cf. §43 on the previous page.
- III. Computes in GL(2,Ẑ)' and GL(2,Ẑ).
- IV. Treats three 'fundamental cases' α_0=1, β_0=1, f=1. It gives lifts K_{1/2}, K_2, K_{-1} and subgroups M^{!~}_{0,3}(q) indexed by q in {0,1,∞,2,−1,1/2}. These are the six points of the S_3-orbit structure of the λ-line: cusps and the 'harmonic' points.
- V–VI. Recapitulation, and the parameters α, β re-expressed via ξ, η.

§47 returns to the homomorphism Π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3} and to 'doubly-tilde' groups M^≈, N^≈, M^{!≈}(0).

§48 'Construction d'un schéma en groupes'. Grothendieck linearises the loop equation. He studies the map α ↦ αρ(α)^{-1} = [β,ρ], then the equation ξ = η ε_1(μ−1) and a group B'_0 = B_{ρ,σ}. Next comes the twisted equation αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1} ε_1(μ−1), defining a group G_{ρ,σ}. Here ρ, σ are apparently finite-order elements: the natural guess is the order-4 and order-6 (or order 2 and 3 projective) generators of SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6.
- He finds a canonical pinning (épinglage) attached to (ρ,σ).
- He studies a sign-twisted equation with ε, works in GP(1), and isolates a condition Tr σ = 0.
- He characterises a 'modular' triple (ε, Γ, ρ).
- He defines group schemes M_{ρ,σ} and So M_{ρ,σ}, with homomorphisms S_oM^{!~}_{0,3} → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/2 and M^{!~}_{0,3} → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Ẑ.
- He gives the structure of M_{ρ,σ} and a canonical homomorphism M_{ρ,σ} → GL(2).
- He analyses radicals R_{ρ,σ}, a subgroup Σ ≅ Z/n × Z/2 × Z/2, dévissages, parameter dictionaries (Y,a,b,μ,ε,ε' versus u,f,α,β,α_0,β_0), and an isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ SΣ*_{ρσ}.
- §48 ends with a 'Rétrospective'.

The next page (§49) generalises to 'groupes M_{ρ,σ} généraux' in a profinite context, with a universal case G* = GL(2,Ẑ). So the programme visible here is roughly: (1) encode the Galois / loop-automorphism data of π̂_{0,3} as solutions of a loop equation in a group with two distinguished torsion elements; (2) construct an algebraic group scheme M_{ρ,σ} whose Ẑ-points receive the profinite GT-like group, modulo centre; (3) analyse it via a map to GL(2), its radical, and finite abelian sign groups.
errors: No mathematical claims are proved on this page (table of contents), so correctness cannot be checked. Internal inconsistencies are only editorial: item XII of §48 is struck through and re-used for 'Rétrospective'; several page numbers are crossed out and replaced; 'repris dans 6°)' marks items 3°–5° as superseded.

ideas.what: Groups of solutions (λ/μ, f, α, β, …) of the 'équation des lacets', describing automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with Γ_Q (M_{0,3}^~, N_{0,3}^{!~}).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s); Grothendieck in Esquisse (1984) as programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the idea; La Longue Marche vol. 1 (Malgoire ed.) covers the earlier part; this second part appears unpublished

ideas.what: Subgroups M^{!~}_{0,3}(q) for q in {0,1,∞,2,−1,1/2}, i.e. stabilisers attached to the cusps and the three harmonic points of the λ-line, with lifts K_{1/2}, K_2, K_{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / S_3-symmetry and harmonic points in GT theory; decomposition-type subgroups

ideas.what: Link of π_{0,3} with SL(2,Z)' and SL(2,Ẑ)', and the identification M_{0,3}^~ = N_{1,1}^~ (genus-0 three-point versus genus-1 one-point).
ideas.modern_name: Legendre/λ-covering relation of M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}; GT acting on SL(2,Z)^ / Γ(2)

ideas.what: Linearisation of the loop equation αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ε_1(μ−1) relative to two torsion elements ρ, σ, and construction of an algebraic group scheme M_{ρ,σ} with canonical pinning, a map to GL(2), radical R_{ρ,σ}, and a sign group Σ ≅ Z/n×Z/2×Z/2.
ideas.modern_name: Unclear; closest: linear/metabelian quotients of GT, or algebraic envelopes of GT-type groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct analogue known to me

ideas.what: Homomorphisms M^{!~}_{0,3} → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Ẑ and S_oM^{!~}_{0,3} → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a GT-like profinite group into the Ẑ-points of an algebraic group

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} from a twisted loop equation in a group with two distinguished torsion elements. He maps a GT-like profinite group into its Ẑ-points modulo centre, then generalises (§49) to arbitrary (G,ρ,σ) with universal case GL(2,Ẑ), with functoriality. A systematic 'algebraic envelope' of GT-type groups attached to SL(2,Z) = Z/4*_{Z/2}Z/6-type data does not, to my knowledge, appear in the GT literature.
missed.quote: 48 Construction d'un schéma en groupes … IX Les groupes M_{ρ,σ} et S_oM_{ρ,σ}, et les homomorphismes S_oM^{!~}_{0,3}→SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/2, M^{!~}_{0,3}→M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Ẑ … X … l'homomorphisme canonique M_{ρ,σ}→Gl(2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a linear-algebraic image or quotient of GT^ in genus 0/1, related to images of GT in Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)) or in GL2-type groups. That is a potentially new invariant or explicit quotient, if the body pages (420–542) bear it out.

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck had already studied subgroups attached to the six special points {0,1,∞,2,−1,1/2} and explicit lifts K_q, plus the identification of the three-point and M_{1,1} 'tilde' groups. This predates the 1990s work of Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and others on GT acting on genus 0 and 1 with these symmetries.
missed.quote: Les sous-groupes M_{0,3}^{!~}(q), q∈{0,1,∞,2,−1,1/2}; Propriétés de M_{0,3}^~ = N_{1,1}^~ (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is priority and history: the genus-1 / SL(2,Z) side of the GT programme was worked out in detail by Grothendieck in unpublished form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a table of contents, but it documents roughly 150 unpublished pages with an apparently original construction: group schemes M_{ρ,σ}, epinglages, a map to GL(2) and sign groups Σ. These receive GT-like groups and have no clear counterpart in the GT literature. The actual content cannot be judged from this page.
transcription_corrections: Line I: superscript on N_{0,3} is '!~' (an exclamation-type mark with tilde), not '♮~'.
§47: target is Ĝ^+_{0,3} (gothic G, as on the previous page), not script E^+.
§48 IX: the prefix written as a small circle subscript is 'So' (as in 'So M_{ρ,σ}' on the next page), i.e. S_oM.
§48 III line: 'et dans Gl(2,Ẑ)' with an insertion 'moyen des' above; the page number 395 is followed by 396 for this item.
§48 2°): includes 'M^+_{ρ,σ}, G^+_{ρ,σ}, C^{+0}_{ρ,σ}'; struck-out first symbol unclear.
